issue_context.analysis: Restoring each recreated tool window to its individual previous zone requires a new stable identity contract. Treating window titles/classes as that identity without evidence could move unrelated windows. This is a feature/compatibility limitation, not a demonstrated localized failure in app-level lookup.
known_information: The maintainer explained one-app history and explicitly warned that recreation order cannot identify individual VS tool windows.
Current AppZoneHistory.GetAppLastZoneIndexSet looks up process path, work area and layout, not a durable per-tool-window identifier.
The report links the VS recreation scenario rather than a supplied stable window identity.
issue_context.summary: App-level zone history cannot promise stable restoration of distinct recreated VS tool windows.
inferences: Different recreation order can defeat order-based restoration; a durable app-provided window identity would be needed to make the promise reliable.
initial_investigation: Read full report and maintainer explanation; inspected current AppZoneHistory lookup keys.
No external VS thread, runtime window identity or current-build recreation was independently verified.

title: FancyZones failing to reposition Visual Studio's recreated tool windows correctly

judgment.recommended_action: Keep the per-window identity limitation explicit; discuss a supported identity design with VS before promising restoration.

comment.body: The current history lookup is scoped to an executable, work area and layout, not an individual recreated VS tool window. The earlier maintainer explanation therefore remains relevant: remembering several zones still would not identify which recreated tool window belongs in which one when creation order changes. We should not infer identity from a changing title or promise that enabling last-known-zone restoration can guarantee this scenario. A reliable per-tool-window feature needs a stable identity contract with VS; no localized bug fix is established here.
